no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it keeps nothing and reads no store. Your AI reads the rows it works over from your lists and hands them in (records); the answer holds the rows to keep for your AI to write.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Sign a person up for an email course after they agreed to it, keep their consent in my records, send the first lesson now and queue the others", and give it email; basis; course; provider.
2. The AI calls do_one_thing_in_my_account at @tools with method tools:run, tool tool:sign-someone-up-for-an-email-course and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Give email, basis (why they may be sent to: { kind: consent, text } with text exactly course.consent_text, only when the person agreed in those words; or { kind: transaction, source_row, at? } naming the purchase or other transaction's row the lessons come with, and its time, from which the lessons are timed (not later than now; without it, from the sign-up)), course (id, public_origin as an https site root, from, mailing_address, 1 to 12 lessons { delay_hours, subject, article_url, text_lines, html_lines? } where every lesson but a receipt carries {{unsubscribeUrl}} and {{mailingAddress}} in each copy it has, the first has delay_hours 0, and a lesson with no html_lines is sent as text only; consent_text and consent_version for a consent basis; optional reply_to (one plain address), checkout_url, stop_path, stop_scope (the stop a person's link makes covers every course of this scope), retry_failed false (a failed send is not tried again), late_after_hours (a lesson more than that past its time is held, not sent) and waits true (each send waits on the caller's waits_until)), enrollment_key (optional; one enrollment per course and key, so two purchases by one address are two enrollments; required when the course waits; without it, one per course and contact), waits_until (true or false, required when the course waits: false queues even the first lesson), variables (optional, this enrollment's own { name: text }, at most 20, filled into its lessons' subject and words; never articleUrl, checkoutUrl, unsubscribeUrl or mailingAddress), source (where they signed up, optional), records (the person's rows listed in its schema, read from their store) and provider (the id of the email provider row in read-data/message-providers.json that the person's email connection is; region too when that row asks for one). Nothing is sent without a basis, a sender and a mailing address. Works out the enrollment row with its basis, time and source and each later lesson's queue row at its time (tool:send-due-email-lessons sends them), and answers them in keep for the caller to write; nothing is kept here; sends lesson 1 with List-Unsubscribe headers unless the enrollment is waiting; a fresh consent lifts an earlier stop of its scope, a transaction never does; signing up again with the same key sends nothing twice. Answers { status: enrolled, already_enrolled }.
4. It keeps nothing and has no records door: it works over the rows you hand in (records) and answers the rows to keep (keep), each with the row it expected, for your AI to write to your store.
